title: France and Spain Face New Heatwaves as Wildfires Continue to Burn
subtitle: Authorities warn of extreme danger as firefighters struggle to control historic forest fires near cities and tourist areas.

summary.en: France and Spain are preparing for another wave of extreme heat that threatens to make ongoing wildfires worse. Thousands of people have been forced to leave their homes and tourist sites to stay safe. Leaders in both countries describe these fires as the most difficult in recent history. While some fires have been contained, others remain unpredictable and dangerous. Officials are now calling for international cooperation to manage these massive disasters.
summary.zh: 法國與西班牙正準備迎接另一波極端高溫，這恐將使持續中的野火惡化。數千人被迫離開家園與旅遊景點以確保安全。兩國領導人皆形容這些火災是近代史上最艱鉅的挑戰。雖然部分火勢已獲控制，但其他火災仍充滿不可預測性與危險。官員們目前正呼籲國際合作，以應對這些大規模災難。

paragraphs.en: France and Spain are currently bracing for a new round of extreme heat, with temperatures expected to rise above 40C in several regions. This weather is making it very difficult for firefighters to control massive wildfires that have been burning for days. According to the BBC, the severe weather is expected to last until at least Sunday, and officials have warned of an extreme risk of new fires starting.
paragraphs.zh: 法國與西班牙目前正嚴陣以待，準備迎接新一波極端高溫，多個地區氣溫預計將突破攝氏四十度。這種天氣讓消防人員極難控制已經延燒數日的森林大火。根據英國廣播公司（BBC）報導，這波惡劣天氣預計至少會持續到週日，官員也警告引發新火災的風險極高。

paragraphs.en: In France, the situation near the city of Bordeaux is particularly worrying. The mayor of Bordeaux, Thomas Cazenave, said he is preparing for all possibilities as one fire is now only 15 kilometers away from the city. President Emmanuel Macron visited the Gironde region and described the situation as the toughest wildfire event the country has faced since World War Two. The French Prime Minister, Sébastien Lecornu, noted that the country is going through an unprecedented fire season, with over 13,000 fire starts recorded since January.
paragraphs.zh: 在法國，波爾多市（Bordeaux）附近的局勢尤其令人擔憂。波爾多市長卡澤納夫（Thomas Cazenave）表示，由於其中一場火災距離市區僅剩十五公里，他正為各種可能性做好準備。法國總統馬克宏（Emmanuel Macron）視察了吉倫特省（Gironde），並形容這是該國自第二次世界大戰以來所面臨最艱鉅的野火事件。法國總理勒科爾尼（Sébastien Lecornu）指出，法國正經歷前所未有的火災季節，自一月以來已記錄到超過一萬三千起火災。

paragraphs.en: Many people have been forced to leave their homes to stay safe. The BBC reported that about 220,000 people have been evacuated in France, while more than 100,000 have left their homes in Spain. The Guardian added that nearly 4,000 people were recently moved from tourist sites near the French coast, including campsites and holiday villages. This was a precautionary measure because winds and heat made the fires harder to control.
paragraphs.zh: 許多民眾被迫離開家園以確保安全。BBC 報導稱，法國約有二十二萬人撤離，西班牙則有超過十萬人離開住處。《衛報》（The Guardian）補充，近期有近四千人從法國海岸附近的旅遊景點撤離，包括露營區與度假村。這是一項預防性措施，因為強風與高溫使得火勢更難控制。

paragraphs.en: In Spain, the situation is also very serious. The country has been in a national emergency for several days as fires burn west of Madrid. Satellite images analyzed by the BBC show that several smaller fires merged into one massive blaze, affecting more than 27,000 hectares of land. The Guardian reported that a fire in the hilly terrain of Ávila has become the largest on record for Spain, burning 50,000 hectares. A firefighter named Javier García told the Associated Press that he had never seen anything like it in his twenty years of work. He explained that the power of the flames is forcing crews to change their tactics, focusing mostly on moving people to safety rather than trying to stop the fire directly.
paragraphs.zh: 在西班牙，情況同樣非常嚴峻。該國已進入國家緊急狀態數日，火勢在馬德里以西蔓延。BBC 分析的衛星影像顯示，幾場較小的火災合併成一場巨大的烈焰，影響面積超過兩萬七千公頃。《衛報》報導，發生在阿維拉（Ávila）丘陵地帶的火災已成為西班牙史上規模最大的一場，燃燒面積達五萬公頃。一名名為賈西亞（Javier García）的消防員告訴美聯社，他在二十年的職涯中從未見過這種景象。他解釋，火焰的威力迫使救災隊改變戰術，將重心放在協助民眾撤離，而非試圖直接撲滅火勢。

paragraphs.en: There is a debate about why these fires are happening. While some fires are caused by accidents like cigarette butts or outdoor cooking, others are being investigated as intentional. The French Prime Minister noted that 162 people have been arrested since July 6 in connection with starting fires. Meanwhile, in Spain, politicians are arguing about the role of climate change in making these disasters more frequent and powerful. While the Spanish Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, has spoken about the urgency of the climate emergency, there is no total agreement on how to best manage the land to prevent future fires.
paragraphs.zh: 關於這些火災發生的原因，各界存在爭論。雖然部分火災是由菸蒂或戶外烹飪等意外引起，但其他火災正被調查是否為人為縱火。法國總理指出，自七月六日以來，已有一百六十二人因涉嫌縱火被捕。與此同時，西班牙政界人士正針對氣候變遷在導致災難頻發與加劇方面的角色進行辯論。儘管西班牙總理桑傑士（Pedro Sánchez）已談及氣候緊急狀態的迫切性，但對於如何妥善管理土地以預防未來火災，各方尚未達成共識。

paragraphs.en: As the heat returns, the work of firefighters remains dangerous. Jerome Steffe, the mayor of Cestas in France, described the situation as the fire of the century. He explained that even when fires seem to slow down, they can suddenly change direction because of the wind or flying embers. This makes the job of protecting homes and towns very difficult.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著高溫回歸，消防人員的工作依然危險。法國塞斯塔（Cestas）市長史蒂芬（Jerome Steffe）將此情況形容為「世紀大火」。他解釋，即使火勢看似減緩，也可能因為風向或飛散的火星而突然改變方向，這使得保護家園與城鎮的工作變得極為困難。

paragraphs.en: To help manage these crises, the European Union has stepped in. An EU spokesperson, Anna-Kaisa Itkonen, stated that planes and helicopters from different member countries have been sent to help France and Spain. She emphasized that no single country has enough resources to handle such large disasters on its own. The EU has warned that some wildfires could potentially continue to burn until early November if the dry and hot conditions persist.
paragraphs.zh: 為了協助處理這些危機，歐盟（European Union）已介入支援。歐盟發言人伊特科寧（Anna-Kaisa Itkonen）表示，已派遣來自不同成員國的飛機與直升機協助法國與西班牙。她強調，沒有任何單一國家有足夠的資源能獨自應對如此大規模的災難。歐盟警告，若乾燥炎熱的氣候持續，部分野火可能會持續燃燒至十一月初。

paragraphs.en: Despite the difficult news, there are small signs of progress. The Guardian reported that Spanish authorities were able to end evacuation orders for 15 municipalities on Tuesday. Prime Minister Sánchez mentioned that they are starting to see light at the end of the tunnel. However, with temperatures set to rise again, officials in both France and Spain are telling the public to remain humble and cautious. The fight against these historic fires is far from over, and the coming weeks will likely remain a difficult test for the region.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管消息艱難，仍有一些小小的進展跡象。《衛報》報導，西班牙當局已於週二解除十五個市鎮的撤離令。總理桑傑士提到，他們開始看見隧道盡頭的曙光。然而，隨著氣溫即將再次升高，法國與西班牙的官員皆呼籲大眾保持謙卑與謹慎。對抗這些歷史性大火的戰役遠未結束，未來幾週對該地區而言，恐將持續是一場艱難的考驗。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To prepare yourself for something difficult or unpleasant that is going to happen.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 準備應對（困難或不愉快的事）。
keyTerms.noteZh: Brace 常見作名詞（支架），這裡指心理或行動上的準備。文中：France and Spain are currently bracing for a new round of extreme heat, with temperatures expected to rise above 40C in several regions.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To combine or join together to form a single entity.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常用於商業（公司合併），這裡指火勢匯聚。文中：Satellite images analyzed by the BBC show that several smaller fires merged into one massive blaze, affecting more than 27,000 hectares of land.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To become involved in a difficult situation or argument in order to help.
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思是「走進去」，這裡指介入處理危機。文中：To help manage these crises, the European Union has stepped in.

keyTerms.term: light at the end of the tunnel
keyTerms.definitionEn: A sign that a difficult period is coming to an end.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 隧道盡頭的曙光（指困境即將結束的跡象）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是慣用語，不能拆開字面解釋。文中：Prime Minister Sánchez mentioned that they are starting to see light at the end of the tunnel.

previousArticles.title: Wildfires Force Mass Evacuations in France and Spain
previousArticles.summaryEn: Massive wildfires are currently burning across France and Spain, forcing hundreds of thousands of people to leave their homes. French authorities are struggling to control a large fire near the city of Bordeaux. In Spain, the government has declared a national state of emergency due to the severity of the situation. Experts note that these fires are behaving in new and unpredictable ways, making them difficult to stop. Officials are now working to provide shelter and safety for the large number of people affected.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary reason why firefighters in Spain have shifted their tactical focus?

options.A: They are waiting for more planes and helicopters to arrive from other EU countries.
options.B: The intensity of the flames has made it safer and more practical to prioritize evacuation over direct suppression.
options.C: They have been ordered to focus on preserving tourist sites rather than rural land.
options.D: The fires have become too small to justify using heavy equipment like water-dropping aircraft.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第四段，消防員 Javier García 表示，火焰的威力強大到迫使團隊改變戰術，將重心放在撤離民眾而非直接滅火。選項 A 雖然提到歐盟支援，但這並非改變戰術的原因。選項 C 錯誤，因為撤離遊客是預防措施，而非戰術核心。選項 D 與文中提到的「massive blaze」和「largest on record」相矛盾。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the challenges faced by local authorities in managing these wildfires?

options.A: The fires are primarily caused by climate change, leaving local governments with no control over the situation.
options.B: Most wildfires are caused by intentional arson, making it impossible to prevent them through better land management.
options.C: The unpredictability of weather conditions and the scale of the disasters exceed the capacity of individual nations.
options.D: The evacuation orders are likely to be permanent for many municipalities due to the severity of the damage.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第七段，歐盟發言人強調沒有任何單一國家有足夠資源獨自處理如此大規模的災難，且第六段提到風向與餘燼會導致火勢突然轉向，顯示了災害的不可預測性。選項 A 說法過於絕對，文中提到原因尚有爭議。選項 B 錯誤，文中提到原因多元，包含意外與人為。選項 D 錯誤，文章最後一段提到已有 15 個市鎮解除了撤離令，顯示撤離並非永久。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, the phrase 'remain humble' is used by officials. What does this imply in the context of the wildfire crisis?

options.A: To acknowledge the power of nature and avoid overconfidence despite minor progress.
options.B: To apologize to the public for the government's inability to stop the fires sooner.
options.C: To keep their public speeches quiet and avoid discussing the political debate.
options.D: To accept that they have failed in their duties and should resign from their positions.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境下，「remain humble」意指即便看到一絲曙光（light at the end of the tunnel），官員仍提醒大眾不要掉以輕心，要對大自然的威力保持敬畏。選項 B、C、D 皆曲解了「humble」在面對自然災害時的正面警示意義，並非指道歉、保持安靜或辭職。

quiz.question: Which of the following best summarizes the central message of the article?

options.A: France and Spain are working together to identify the arsonists responsible for the recent fires.
options.B: The historical record of wildfires in Europe shows that the current season is the most destructive ever.
options.C: Despite international aid and some progress, France and Spain face a persistent and dangerous battle against extreme wildfires.
options.D: Climate change is the sole reason for the record-breaking wildfires currently devastating the European continent.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文全面涵蓋了法國與西班牙的火災現況、消防員的挑戰、歐盟的支援以及對未來的展望。選項 A 僅是文章的一小部分細節。選項 B 雖然提到歷史紀錄，但並非全文主旨。選項 D 錯誤，因為文章明確指出火災原因存在爭議（包含意外、人為與氣候變遷），並非單一因素造成。
